title: PHINE - Phthalate and Iodine in Neonates. Urine screening for plasticizers (phthalates) and iodine in newborns and their mothers
summary:
The study will analyse the urine of mature newborns and their mothers for phthalate and iodine concentrations.  We want to investigate the exposure to endocrine active substances and identify predisposing factors that could influence both phthalate exposure and iodine status.
The study is prospective and monocentric and will be conducted at St Elisabeth Hospital Bochum. It is planned to recruit 100 mother-child pairs in the first few days after birth. In addition, information on socio-demographic data, nutrition, supplementation behaviour and the use of personal hygiene products will be collected via questionnaires and medical records. The background to the study is, on the one hand, the declining trend in iodine supply in Germany and, on the other hand, the increased detection of phthalates in the urine of children in Germany. The hypothesis for the iodine study is that newborns born to mothers without adherent iodine supplementation are significantly more likely to have an insufficient iodine concentration (<100 µg/L) in their urine than newborns born to mothers with adherent iodine supplementation. For the phthalate part, we assume that the frequency of positive detections in newborns is significantly higher in mothers who used potentially risky substances during pregnancy or shortly before birth.
conditions: No explicit diseases are being investigated, but rather serious adverse health effects that could be caused by an iodine deficiency or a high phthalate concentration in newborns.

interventions.name: The prevalence of phthlate metabolites in the urine of newborns and their mothers is measured. The results of the questionnaire are used to analyse a possible correlation between the use of potentially risky substances during pregnancy and the measurements.

The prevalence of an insufficient iodine supply in the urine of newborns and their mothers is measured in parallel. The results of the questionnaire are used to analyse a possible correlation between supplementation behaviour during pregnancy and the measurement results.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written consent of the mothers 
- Age of majority of the mother 
- No prematurity of the newborn (from the completed 37th week of pregnancy)
- Newborns without pre-existing conditions (treatment on the peripheral labour ward, no transfer required)
- Inpatient stay
Exclusion criteria:
All cases are excluded,
- in which the mother does not agree to participate in the study,
- where the mother is not of legal age,
- where the mother is unable to provide information for linguistic, psychological or somatic reasons,
- where the child was born before the 37th week of pregnancy,
- where the child is classified by the hospital staff as ill or requiring intensive monitoring (no treatment on the peripheral labour ward).
